Pass rush efficiency is modeled as a conditional expectation difference in EPA given player presence. Defensive line alignment is treated as a binary choice effect on EPA, with 3-tech vs 5-tech configurations forming a dichotomy. Opponent series outcomes are aggregated into a weighted sum of discrete outcomes, each contributing to overall defensive strength. These primitives form a hierarchical Bayesian network where EPA acts as a latent variable linking player-level performance to macro-defensive effectiveness. The failure mode arises when data integrity issues (e.g., obscured values, misidentified teams) corrupt the likelihood functions used in Bayesian inference, leading to spurious conclusions about defensive strategy efficacy.
